records.source: Καὶ σημεῖον μέγα ὤφθη ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, γυνὴ περιβεβλημένη τὸν ἥλιον, καὶ ἡ σελήνη ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐπὶ τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτῆς στέφανος ἀστέρων δώδεκα, καὶ ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα· καὶ κράζει ὠδίνουσα καὶ βασανιζομένη τεκεῖν.
records.gloss: And a sign great appeared in the heaven, a woman having been clothed with the sun, and the moon under the feet of her, and on the head of her a crown of stars twelve, \v 2 and in womb having, and she cries out being in labor and being in pain to give birth.
pieces: A great sign was seen in the sky: a woman wearing the sun as her clothing, the moon beneath her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.
She was with child, and she cried out in labor, in agony to give birth.

L.1: And a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars,
L.2: and she was pregnant, and she cries out in labor and in agony to give birth.

R.1: Then a great sign appeared in the sky. It was a woman dressed with the sun. The moon was under her feet, and on her head she wore a crown of twelve stars.
R.2: She was about to have a baby, and she cried out in pain.

decisions.choice: a sign: a picture that points beyond itself
decisions.reason: σημεῖον means a sign or portent. What John sees is a vision whose meaning lies beyond the picture.

decisions.choice: the woman: God's people, from whom the Messiah comes
decisions.reason: In Joseph's dream the sun, moon and eleven stars stand for Jacob's family, the people of Israel (Genesis 37:9-10), and the prophets picture Zion as a woman in labor (Isaiah 26:17; 66:7-8; Micah 4:10). The woman gives birth to the Messiah (12:5), and her other children are those who hold to the testimony of Jesus (12:17). So she most likely stands for the people of God, Israel and then the church. Christian tradition has also seen Mary in her, and she is the one through whom the child is born. The text does not name the woman.

decisions.choice: sign
decisions.reason: Sign is a key term and stays the same at every level.

records.heading: The woman and the dragon

records.source: καὶ ὤφθη ἄλλο σημεῖον ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, καὶ ἰδοὺ δράκων μέγας πυρρός, ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ καὶ κέρατα δέκα καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ἑπτὰ διαδήματα, καὶ ἡ οὐρὰ αὐτοῦ σύρει τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀστέρων τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἔβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν γῆν.
records.gloss: And appeared another sign in the heaven, and behold a dragon great fiery-red having heads seven and horns ten and on the heads of him seven diadems, \v 4 and the tail of him drags the third of the stars of the heaven, and he threw them to the earth.
pieces: And another sign was seen in the sky: look, a great dragon, red as fire, with seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven royal crowns.
With his tail he drags away a third of the stars of heaven, and he threw them down to the earth.

L.3: And another sign appeared in heaven, and look, a great fiery red dragon having seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven royal crowns,
L.4: and his tail drags away a third of the stars of heaven, and he threw them to the earth.

R.3: Then another sign appeared in the sky. It was a huge red dragon. He had seven heads and ten horns, and a king's crown on each head.
R.4: His tail swept away a third of the stars from the sky and threw them down to the earth.

decisions.choice: the dragon: Satan, with the marks of the beasts of Daniel
decisions.reason: Revelation names the dragon in 12:9: he is the devil and Satan. The Old Testament speaks of a sea monster, Leviathan, as God's enemy (Isaiah 27:1; Psalm 74:13-14). The ten horns come from the fourth beast of Daniel 7:7, and the beast of 13:1 has the same heads and horns. His red color may suggest bloodshed (compare 6:4).

decisions.choice: diadems: crowns of royal power
decisions.reason: διαδήματα is the crown of a king, a band worn as a sign of royal rule, unlike the victor's wreath of 2:10 and 4:4. The dragon claims kingly power.

decisions.choice: stars thrown down: Daniel 8:10
decisions.reason: In Daniel 8:10 the little horn grows great and throws some of the host of heaven and of the stars to the ground. The stars may stand for angels who fell with the dragon (12:9), or for God's people whom he attacks.

decisions.choice: royal crowns (L, B); a king's crown (R)
decisions.reason: "Royal crowns" shows the difference from the victor's wreath (m2).

decisions.choice: he, his: the dragon
decisions.reason: The dragon is Satan (12:9), a person, so every level calls him "he".

records.source: καὶ ὁ δράκων ἕστηκεν ἐνώπιον τῆς γυναικὸς τῆς μελλούσης τεκεῖν, ἵνα ὅταν τέκῃ τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς καταφάγῃ.
records.gloss: And the dragon stands before the woman the [one] being about to give birth, so that when she gives birth the child of her he might devour.
pieces: Before the woman who was about to give birth the dragon stood waiting, ready to devour her child the moment the child was born.

L.4: And the dragon stands before the woman who is about to give birth, so that when she gives birth he might devour her child.

R.4: The dragon stood in front of the woman who was about to give birth. He wanted to eat her baby as soon as the baby was born.

decisions.choice: the enemy waits to destroy the child
decisions.reason: Pharaoh ordered the Hebrew boys killed at birth (Exodus 1:15-22), and Herod tried to kill the child Jesus (Matthew 2:13-18). The dragon stands behind such attacks.

decisions.choice: stands: a vivid perfect
decisions.reason: ἕστηκεν is perfect with a present sense: he has taken his stand and waits.

records.source: καὶ ἔτεκεν υἱόν, ἄρσεν, ὃς μέλλει ποιμαίνειν πάντα τὰ ἔθνη ἐν ῥάβδῳ σιδηρᾷ· καὶ ἡρπάσθη τὸ τέκνον αὐτῆς πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ πρὸς τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: And she gave birth to a son, a male, who is about to shepherd all the nations with a rod iron; and was caught up the child of her to the God and to the throne of him.
pieces: She bore a son, a boy, the one who is to shepherd all the nations with a rod of iron; and her child was caught up to God, to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne.

L.5: And she gave birth to a son, a male [child], who is going to shepherd all the nations with an iron rod, and her child was caught up to God and to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne.

R.5: She gave birth to a son, a baby boy. He will rule all the nations with an iron rod. Her child was taken up to God and to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne.

decisions.choice: to shepherd the nations with a rod of iron: Psalm 2:9
decisions.reason: The words come from Psalm 2:9, the psalm of God's anointed king, quoted already in 2:27. The child is the Messiah. υἱόν ἄρσεν, "a son, a male", echoes Isaiah 66:7, where Zion gives birth to a male child.

decisions.choice: caught up to God: from birth to ascension
decisions.reason: The story leaps from the Messiah's birth to his being taken up to God's throne. His life, death and resurrection are not told here, but 12:11 speaks of "the blood of the Lamb". The dragon fails: the child is beyond his reach.

decisions.choice: shepherd (L, B); rule (R)
decisions.reason: As in 2:27.

records.source: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἔφυγεν εἰς τὴν ἔρημον, ὅπου ἔχει ἐκεῖ τόπον ἡτοιμασμένον ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα ἐκεῖ τρέφωσιν αὐτὴν ἡμέρας χιλίας διακοσίας ἑξήκοντα.
records.gloss: And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has there a place having been prepared by the God, so that there they may nourish her days 1,260.
pieces: As for the woman, she fled into the wilderness. There God has a place ready for her, where she is to be fed for 1,260 days.

L.6: And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that there they may nourish her 1,260 days.

R.6: The woman ran away into the desert. God had prepared a place for her there. She would be taken care of there for 1,260 days.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: a place of refuge where God provides
decisions.reason: Israel was fed with manna in the wilderness after the exodus (Exodus 16), and Elijah was fed there when he fled (1 Kings 17:2-6; 19:3-8). The wilderness is a hard place, but God keeps his people there.

decisions.choice: 1,260 days: the time of trial
decisions.reason: See the note on 11:2-3. It is the same as "a time, times and half a time" in 12:14.

decisions.choice: they may nourish: no subject named
decisions.reason: τρέφωσιν "they nourish" has no subject; it means that she will be fed and cared for, by God's provision.

records.source: Καὶ ἐγένετο πόλεμος ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ, ὁ Μιχαὴλ καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ τοῦ πολεμῆσαι μετὰ τοῦ δράκοντος.
records.gloss: And there was war in the heaven, the Michael and the angels of him to make war with the dragon.
pieces: And there was war in heaven: Michael and his angels went to battle against the dragon.

L.7: And war broke out in heaven: Michael and his angels [went] to make war with the dragon.

R.7: Then there was a war in heaven. Michael and his angels fought against the dragon.

decisions.choice: Michael: the archangel who protects God's people
decisions.reason: In Daniel, Michael is "one of the chief princes" and "the great prince who protects your people" (Daniel 10:13, 21; 12:1). Jude 9 calls him the archangel.

decisions.choice: an unusual construction
decisions.reason: The Greek has the names in the subject form followed by an infinitive with the article, "Michael and his angels to make war". It may reflect a Hebrew way of saying "had to fight" or "went out to fight".

records.heading: War in heaven

records.source: καὶ ὁ δράκων ἐπολέμησεν καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν, οὐδὲ τόπος εὑρέθη αὐτῶν ἔτι ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ.
records.gloss: And the dragon made war and the angels of him, \v 8 and not he was strong, nor place was found of them still in the heaven.
pieces: The dragon and his angels fought back,
but he was not strong enough, and there was no longer any place for them in heaven.

L.7: And the dragon and his angels made war,
L.8: and he was not strong enough, nor was a place found for them any longer in heaven.

R.7: The dragon and his angels fought back.
R.8: But the dragon was not strong enough. There was no more room for them in heaven.

decisions.choice: no place was found for them: Daniel 2:35
decisions.reason: When the stone destroyed the statue of the kingdoms, "no trace of them could be found" (Daniel 2:35; compare Revelation 20:11). The dragon has lost his place in heaven.

records.source: καὶ ἐβλήθη ὁ δράκων ὁ μέγας, ὁ ὄφις ὁ ἀρχαῖος, ὁ καλούμενος Διάβολος καὶ ὁ Σατανᾶς, ὁ πλανῶν τὴν οἰκουμένην ὅλην ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν, καὶ οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἐβλήθησαν.
records.gloss: And was thrown the dragon the great, the serpent the ancient, the [one] being called Devil and the Satan, the [one] deceiving the inhabited world whole, he was thrown to the earth, and the angels of him with him were thrown.
pieces: Down went the great dragon, cast out: the serpent of old, the one called the devil and Satan, deceiver of the whole world. He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down along with him.

L.9: And the great dragon was thrown down, the ancient serpent, who is called [the] Devil and Satan, the deceiver of the whole world; he was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him.

R.9: The great dragon was thrown out of heaven. He is the ancient snake called the devil and Satan. He fools the whole world. He was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were thrown down with him.

decisions.choice: the ancient serpent: Genesis 3
decisions.reason: The serpent deceived the woman in the garden (Genesis 3:1-15), and God promised enmity between the serpent and the woman's offspring. Here the serpent is unmasked as the devil.

decisions.choice: devil and Satan: slanderer and adversary
decisions.reason: "Devil" means slanderer, "Satan" (from Hebrew) means adversary or accuser (Job 1-2; Zechariah 3:1-2). Both names fit his work of accusing (12:10) and deceiving.

decisions.choice: thrown down from heaven: Jesus's words
decisions.reason: Jesus said, "I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven" (Luke 10:18), and "now the ruler of this world will be cast out" (John 12:31). The defeat is linked with Christ's victory (12:10-11).

decisions.choice: Devil (L); devil (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal capitalizes as a name; Balanced and Readable use lowercase "the devil", as English Bibles usually do.

records.source: Καὶ ἤκουσα φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ λέγουσαν· Ἄρτι ἐγένετο ἡ σωτηρία καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν καὶ ἡ ἐξουσία τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐβλήθη ὁ κατήγωρ τῶν ἀδελφῶν ἡμῶν, ὁ κατηγορῶν αὐτοὺς ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός.
records.gloss: And I heard a voice great in the heaven saying: Now has come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of the God of us and the authority of the Christ of him, because was thrown down the accuser of the brothers of us, the [one] accusing them before the God of us day and night.
pieces: I heard a loud voice in heaven: "The time has come! Salvation is here, and power, and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}; for the one who accused our {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, accusing them day and night before our God, has been cast out.

L.10: And I heard a loud voice in heaven saying, "Now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God and the authority of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, because the accuser of our {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} has been thrown down, who accuses them before our God day and night.

R.10: Then I heard a loud voice in heaven say, "Now God has saved {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people! Now our God shows {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power and rules as king, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} has authority. The one who accused our {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} has been thrown out. Day and night he accused them in front of our God.

decisions.choice: salvation, power, kingdom and authority: God's victory made known
decisions.reason: σωτηρία here, as in 7:10, is God's deliverance and victory. The kingdom announced at the seventh trumpet (11:15) is proclaimed again: Satan's fall shows that God reigns and Christ has authority.

decisions.choice: the accuser: Satan as prosecutor
decisions.reason: κατήγωρ is a legal word for a prosecutor. In Job 1-2 and Zechariah 3:1 Satan accuses God's people before God. After Christ's death there is no case left against them (Romans 8:33-34).

decisions.choice: our brothers and sisters: believers
decisions.reason: The voice in heaven calls the believers on earth "our brothers and sisters". The speakers may be the martyrs or other heavenly worshipers (compare 6:11; 19:10).

decisions.choice: salvation (L, B); God has saved (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the verb, which the key-term list allows (7:10).

decisions.choice: brothers and sisters | brothers
decisions.reason: The word includes all believers.

records.source: καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐνίκησαν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸ αἷμα τοῦ ἀρνίου καὶ διὰ τὸν λόγον τῆς μαρτυρίας αὐτῶν, καὶ οὐκ ἠγάπησαν τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτῶν ἄχρι θανάτου·
records.gloss: And they overcame him because of the blood of the Lamb and because of the word of the testimony of them, and not they loved the life of them until death.
pieces: They have overcome him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony; they did not hold their lives dear, even in the face of death.

L.11: And they overcame him because of the blood of the Lamb and because of the word of their testimony, and they did not love their life until death.

R.11: Our {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} won the victory over him. They won because the Lamb gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood, and because they kept telling the truth about Jesus. They did not love their own lives so much that they were afraid to die.

decisions.choice: they overcame: the victory of the Lamb shared by his people
decisions.reason: ἐνίκησαν is the "overcome" of the seven letters (2:7). The believers' victory rests on the Lamb's death, which took away the accuser's case, and on their faithful witness. They win as he won, by faithfulness unto death (5:5-6).

decisions.choice: not loving their life: Jesus's teaching
decisions.reason: Jesus said that whoever loves their life will lose it, and whoever loses it for his sake will keep it (Mark 8:35; John 12:25). ψυχὴν means life, the person's own self.

decisions.choice: overcame (L); have overcome (B); won the victory (R)
decisions.reason: The same word as in the letters (2:7).

decisions.choice: Our brothers and sisters (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are (12:10).

records.source: διὰ τοῦτο εὐφραίνεσθε, οἱ οὐρανοὶ καὶ οἱ ἐν αὐτοῖς σκηνοῦντες.
records.gloss: Because of this rejoice, the heavens and those in them dwelling.
pieces: So rejoice, you heavens, and all who live in them!

L.12: Therefore rejoice, heavens, and you who dwell in them!

R.12: So be happy, heavens, and everyone who lives there!

decisions.choice: rejoice, heavens: the psalms and Isaiah
decisions.reason: "Sing for joy, O heavens" (Isaiah 44:23; 49:13; compare Psalm 96:11). σκηνοῦντες is the verb of dwelling in a tent, used of God's presence in 7:15.

records.source: οὐαὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν, ὅτι κατέβη ὁ διάβολος πρὸς ὑμᾶς, ἔχων θυμὸν μέγαν, εἰδὼς ὅτι ὀλίγον καιρὸν ἔχει.
records.gloss: Woe the earth and the sea, because came down the devil to you having fury great, knowing that little time he has.
pieces: Woe to earth and sea, because the devil has gone down to you full of fury, knowing that the time left to him is short."

L.12: Woe to the earth and the sea, because the devil has come down to you with great fury, knowing that he has [only] a short time."

R.12: But how terrible it will be for the earth and the sea! The devil has come down to you, and he is very angry. He knows that he has only a little time left."

decisions.choice: a short time: the limited time of 12:6 and 12:14
decisions.reason: καιρὸν is time as a set season. The devil knows his time is limited, the three and a half years of the woman's refuge. His rage is that of a defeated enemy.

decisions.choice: Woe (L, B); how terrible (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:13.

records.source: Καὶ ὅτε εἶδεν ὁ δράκων ὅτι ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν, ἐδίωξεν τὴν γυναῖκα ἥτις ἔτεκεν τὸν ἄρσενα.
records.gloss: And when saw the dragon that he was thrown to the earth, he pursued the woman who gave birth to the male.
pieces: Seeing that he had been thrown down to the earth, the dragon hunted the woman who had borne the boy.

L.13: And when the dragon saw that he had been thrown down to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male [child].

R.13: When the dragon saw that he had been thrown down to the earth, he chased the woman who had given birth to the boy.

decisions.choice: pursued: hunted and persecuted
decisions.reason: ἐδίωξεν means to pursue and also to persecute. Unable to reach the child, the dragon turns on the woman.

records.heading: The dragon pursues the woman

records.source: καὶ ἐδόθησαν τῇ γυναικὶ αἱ δύο πτέρυγες τοῦ ἀετοῦ τοῦ μεγάλου, ἵνα πέτηται εἰς τὴν ἔρημον εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῆς, ὅπου τρέφεται ἐκεῖ καιρὸν καὶ καιροὺς καὶ ἥμισυ καιροῦ ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ ὄφεως.
records.gloss: And were given to the woman the two wings of the eagle the great, so that she might fly into the wilderness into the place of her, where she is nourished there a time and times and half of a time from face of the serpent.
pieces: The woman was given the two wings of the great eagle to fly to her place in the wilderness, where she is cared for, away from the serpent, for a time, and times, and half a time.

L.14: And the two wings of the great eagle were given to the woman, so that she might fly into the wilderness, to her place, where she is nourished for a time and times and half a time, away from the face of the serpent.

R.14: The woman was given two wings like those of a great eagle. She flew to her place in the desert. There she was taken care of for three and a half years, safe from the snake.

decisions.choice: eagle's wings: God's rescue at the exodus
decisions.reason: God told Israel, "I bore you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself" (Exodus 19:4; compare Deuteronomy 32:11; Isaiah 40:31). The woman is carried to safety as Israel was.

decisions.choice: a time, times and half a time: Daniel 7:25 and 12:7
decisions.reason: Daniel's phrase means three and a half years (one, two and a half), the same span as 1,260 days (12:6) and forty-two months (11:2; 13:5).

decisions.choice: a time and times and half a time (L, B); three and a half years (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep Daniel's phrase; Readable gives its meaning (m2).

records.source: καὶ ἔβαλεν ὁ ὄφις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ὀπίσω τῆς γυναικὸς ὕδωρ ὡς ποταμόν, ἵνα αὐτὴν ποταμοφόρητον ποιήσῃ.
records.gloss: And threw the serpent out of the mouth of him after the woman water as a river, so that her swept-away-by-river he might make.
pieces: Then out of his mouth the serpent poured water after the woman, like a river, to have her carried off by the flood.

L.15: And the serpent threw water like a river out of his mouth after the woman, so that he might make her swept away by the river.

R.15: Then the snake poured out water from his mouth like a river. He wanted the flood to carry the woman away.

decisions.choice: a flood: overwhelming danger
decisions.reason: In the psalms floods and torrents stand for deadly danger and the attacks of enemies (Psalm 18:5, 17; 124:4-5; Isaiah 43:2). The serpent tries to overwhelm God's people.

records.source: καὶ ἐβοήθησεν ἡ γῆ τῇ γυναικί, καὶ ἤνοιξεν ἡ γῆ τὸ στόμα αὐτῆς καὶ κατέπιεν τὸν ποταμὸν ὃν ἔβαλεν ὁ δράκων ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ·
records.gloss: And helped the earth the woman, and opened the earth the mouth of it and swallowed the river which threw the dragon out of the mouth of him.
pieces: But the earth came to the woman's rescue: it opened its mouth and swallowed the river the dragon had poured from his mouth.

L.16: And the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed the river that the dragon had thrown out of his mouth.

R.16: But the earth helped the woman. The ground opened up and swallowed the river that came out of the dragon's mouth.

decisions.choice: the earth opening its mouth
decisions.reason: The earth opened its mouth and swallowed Korah's rebels (Numbers 16:30-32), and after the crossing of the sea "the earth swallowed" the Egyptians (Exodus 15:12). God's creation itself protects his people.

records.source: καὶ ὠργίσθη ὁ δράκων ἐπὶ τῇ γυναικί, καὶ ἀπῆλθεν ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν λοιπῶν τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτῆς, τῶν τηρούντων τὰς ἐντολὰς τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ ἐχόντων τὴν μαρτυρίαν Ἰησοῦ·
records.gloss: And was angry the dragon at the woman, and went away to make war with the rest of the offspring of her, those keeping the commandments of the God and having the testimony of Jesus.
pieces: In his fury against the woman the dragon went off to make war on the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and hold to the testimony of Jesus.

L.17: And the dragon was enraged at the woman and went off to make war with the rest of her offspring, those who keep the commandments of God and hold the testimony of Jesus.

R.17: The dragon was very angry with the woman. So he went to fight against the rest of her children. They are the people who obey God's commands and keep telling the truth about Jesus.

decisions.choice: her offspring: the promise of Genesis 3:15
decisions.reason: God promised enmity between the serpent and the woman, and between his offspring and hers (Genesis 3:15). σπέρματος is the word "seed" or offspring. The rest of her offspring are the followers of Jesus, her firstborn.

decisions.choice: the testimony of Jesus
decisions.reason: See the note on 1:2. They hold to the testimony Jesus gave and bear witness to him.

records.source: καὶ ἐστάθη ἐπὶ τὴν ἄμμον τῆς θαλάσσης.
records.gloss: And he stood on the sand of the sea.
pieces: And the dragon took his stand on the sand of the seashore.

L.18: And he stood on the sand of the sea.

R.18: Then the dragon stood on the beach by the sea.

decisions.choice: he stood: the dragon
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "he stood", so the dragon waits by the sea, from which the beast comes up (13:1). Many later manuscripts read "I stood", making John the one on the shore. Some Bibles number this sentence as the start of 13:1. The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the dragon (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject (m1).
